questions.question: What new claim do the authors make beyond the earlier Nambu–Goto hyperdeterminant result?

options.A: The N=2 Green–Schwarz model in D=2+2 shares the [SL(2,IR)]³ feature after eliminating its zweibein
options.B: The N=2 NSR action is itself a Cayley determinant before eliminating fermions
options.C: The construction extends unchanged to ten-dimensional Type IIB strings
options.D: The hyperdeterminant removes the need for κ-symmetry

questions.rationale: Their central extension is to the classical GS sigma model with D=2+2 target spacetime.
questions.evidence_quote: the same feature is shared by Green-Schwarz σ -model for N = 2 superstring whose target space-time is D = 2+2

questions.question: Why do the authors avoid claiming quantum equivalence to the conventional N=2 NSR string?

options.A: Quantum-level equivalence of Nambu–Goto and Polyakov actions is not well established
options.B: Their action has no fermionic κ-symmetry
options.C: The target superspace has the wrong number of fermions
options.D: The WZNW term is not invariant under world-sheet diffeomorphisms

questions.rationale: They explicitly limit the argument to classical-level symmetries and do not claim quantum equivalence.
questions.evidence_quote: we do not claim the quantum equivalence of our formulation

questions.question: What does the paper say happens to the hidden discrete triality of the pure Nambu–Goto hyperdeterminant when the GS WZNW term is included?

options.A: It is lost because nonzero BAB components mix the three index sectors
options.B: It becomes an exact symmetry of both terms
options.C: It survives only after κ-gauge fixing
options.D: It is replaced by a fourth SL(2,IR) factor

questions.rationale: The NG hyperdeterminant has the exchange symmetry, but the WZNW term breaks it.
questions.evidence_quote: the mixture of Πiα .α and Πiα or Πi .α via the non-zero components of BAB breaks the exchange symmetry

questions.question: Which target-space content does the paper attach to D=(2,2;2,2) superspace?

options.A: Two plus two bosonic coordinates together with two chiral and two antichiral fermionic coordinates
options.B: Two bosonic and two world-sheet fermionic coordinates with N=(2,2) spacetime supersymmetry
options.C: Four bosonic coordinates and four unconstrained Majorana spinors
options.D: Ten bosonic coordinates and two complex Weyl spinors

questions.rationale: The notation denotes the D=2+2 target superspace and N=(1,1) spacetime supersymmetry.
questions.evidence_quote: meaning 2 + 2 bosonic coordinates, plus 2 chiral and 2 anti-chiral fermionic coordinates

questions.question: How is the manifest [SL(2,IR)]³ action organized in the construction?

options.A: It acts on the three pullback indices i, α, and dotted α
options.B: It acts on the two world-sheet coordinates and the target-space metric determinant
options.C: It acts on three independent spacetime vectors in the WZNW term only
options.D: It rotates the two chiral sectors and the κ parameter

questions.rationale: The three indices of Πiα .α carry the three group factors.
questions.evidence_quote: the [SL(2, IR)]3 symmetry acts on the three indices i, α, .α carried by the pull-back

questions.question: What role does the paper assign to Γij=ΠiaΠja after the world-sheet metric is removed?

options.A: It acts as an effective world-sheet metric built from superspace pullbacks
options.B: It is an auxiliary gauge field independent of the embedding coordinates
options.C: It is the target metric whose determinant defines the WZNW term
options.D: It vanishes identically by the Virasoro constraints

questions.rationale: The conclusion identifies Γij as the effective metric in the metric-free formulation.
questions.evidence_quote: the combination Γij ≡ΠiaΠja plays a role of ‘effective metric’ on the 2D world-sheet

questions.question: Why is eliminating gij from the Green–Schwarz action technically nontrivial, yet still possible in the authors' derivation?

options.A: Its field equation is nonalgebraic because gij reappears through Ω, but substitution yields √−Γ
options.B: Its field equation is algebraic only after imposing the quantum Virasoro constraints
options.C: The metric equation is nonlocal and must be solved numerically
options.D: The WZNW term makes gij complex, so the authors discard it

questions.rationale: Equation (4.3) contains Ω=gijΓij on its right-hand side, but the on-shell lagrangian simplifies to the NG term.
questions.evidence_quote: field equation which is not algebraic.

questions.question: How do the authors establish the κ-invariance cancellation in their metric-free action?

options.A: The NG and WZNW variations cancel after using the built-in Γ++=Γ−−=0 conditions
options.B: Each term is separately invariant without constraints
options.C: A variation of the eliminated zweibein cancels the WZNW variation
options.D: The cancellation follows only after integrating over the extra Vainberg coordinate

questions.rationale: The displayed variation reduces to a term proportional to Π−aΠ−a, which vanishes by the constraints.

questions.question: What condition do the authors say makes their GS action light-cone equivalent to the NSR formulation?

options.B: The presence of the hidden triality symmetry
options.C: The absence of a WZNW term

questions.rationale: They invoke the standard κ-symmetry criterion for light-cone equivalence.
questions.evidence_quote: The existence of fermionic κ-symmetry also guarantees the light-cone equivalence of our system

questions.question: Which spacetime signature rationale do the authors give for favoring D=2+2 in realizing the real [SL(2,IR)]³ symmetry?

options.B: SO(2,2) is compact, whereas SO(3,1) has no spinors
options.C: Only D=2+2 admits a world-sheet metric
options.D: D=2+2 makes dotted and undotted indices complex conjugates

questions.rationale: The paper contrasts the real-factor decomposition in signature (2,2) with the complex group in (3,1).
